name: PT Widodo Makmur Unggas Tbk

frontmatter.title: Widodo Makmur Unggas: the recapitalisation is scheduled, and the equity is still worth nothing
frontmatter.summary: WMUU restructured its debt, not its economics. The rights issue is approved, with the parent contracted as standby buyer for its own loan conversion but only a third of the shares needing cash at twice the market price. Carrying the unallocated cost the previous forecast dropped, the business earns a negative EBITDA, and neither the operating methods nor the closure case clear net debt. SELL.
thesis: The data pack understates depreciation by an order of magnitude; on the audited numbers FY2025 EBITDA is IDR20.4bn against interest of IDR38.6bn, and the forecast earns a negative EBITDA in every year from FY2026 [S0][S10].

The FY2025 segment note shows segment gross profit of IDR31.3bn against a consolidated gross loss of IDR-12.8bn [S10]: a recurring unallocated cost inside cost of goods sold that the previous forecast dropped, which turns forecast EBITDA negative in every year [S10].

The PMHMETD I rights issue was approved in April 2026, OJK-effective in June and scheduled to distribute in July: 6.0 bn new shares at Rp100, IDR600.5bn at the documented maximum. The parent converts its whole 406 IDR bn claim and stands as standby buyer, so only a minority cash leg needs money at twice the market price [S13].

Even crediting that conversion, enterprise value on our DCF is IDR-930.1bn and the closure case gives IDR0.0bn [S0]: both below net debt, so the target is the limited-liability floor, not a point estimate.

Governance is weak: a qualified audit opinion, a court-supervised settlement, an OJK fine for an affiliate-transaction procedure breach, uninsured fixed assets and a parent that is creditor, controlling shareholder, subscriber and standby buyer at once [S2][S9][S10][S13].

catalysts.event: Q3-2026 LK: a filed September quarter that reconciles to the pack, whose Q3 P&L is internally inconsistent, and an explanation of the first-half fall in debt
FY2026 audited accounts: whether the qualified opinion clears and whether the rights shares were ever issued
Deadline the settlement plan sets for completing or divesting the stalled construction projects

blocks.text: **SELL. Target Rp0, a return of -100.0% from Rp49.** The zero is the limited-liability floor, not a point estimate: with the minimum traded price at Rp1 [S8], a holder's realisable loss is the whole investment. This refresh corrects valuation text and documentation; inputs and target are unchanged.

The variant view is the operating line, corrected both ways. The audited accounts show a loss from operations of IDR-45.0bn after depreciation of 65.4 IDR bn, of which IDR5.9bn sits in operating expenses and the rest in cost of goods sold [S10]; the pack carries only the operating-expense slice, so restating both turns its EBITDA loss into a positive IDR20.4bn [S0][S10]. Against that, the segment note shows gross profit of IDR31.3bn against a consolidated gross loss of IDR-12.8bn - a recurring unallocated cost inside cost of goods sold [S10]. Carrying both, forecast EBITDA is IDR-16.1bn in FY2026 and negative in every year to FY2035, against interest of IDR38.9bn [S0][S10].

Three things move the value, none operational: net debt of IDR1,252.5bn at the 2025 year-end, lower at 30 September 2026 after the asset-for-debt exchange, still of the same order as the IDR634.1bn market capitalisation on the pre-issue count [S0][S13]; a revenue path to IDR1,424.1bn by FY2030 on which EBIT stays at IDR-92.0bn, because the earned gross margin of 1.0% sits below the operating-cost block of 8.8% of sales [S0][S10]; and the recapitalisation, contracted but not evidenced [S13]. We are deliberately not cautious - we credit the parent's conversion, which removes its 406 IDR bn loan, assume the demand recovery holds, and assume feed-cost pass-through [S0][S9][S10] - and the equity is still worth nothing.

WMUU is a vertically integrated Indonesian poultry processor - feedmill, breeding and hatchery, broiler farms, slaughter and carcass, and eggs - controlled by PT Widodo Makmur Perkasa, itself listed and separately restructuring its debt [S6][S9]. Carcass is the largest segment: 643 IDR bn of FY2025 revenue of IDR740.9bn, with eggs, day-old chicks, feed and broilers the rest [S10]. It is a commodity - the company buys live birds in the open market and sells meat at a price it does not set - while day-old chicks and feed out-earned it at gross-profit level [S9][S10]. Feedmill output fell to 1,464 t in FY2025, a collapse of feed trading, while hatchery output rose to 4.4 m birds and egg production to 37.3 m eggs; strategy is utilisation and diversification rather than expansion [S9][S10].

It is a sub-scale challenger: no brand, no pricing power, no distribution advantage, selling where the regional price is set by supply [S9][S10]. Its one asset advantage is a large, under-utilised fixed-asset base of 2,124 IDR bn net book value - operating leverage if volumes return, losses if they do not [S10]. The parent holds 40.9% of the shares, is the largest creditor through a 406 IDR bn shareholder loan and subscribes to the rights issue by converting that claim at Rp100 against a Rp49 market [S0][S13].

The Indonesian poultry chain runs from imported feed grains through feedmills to breeding, hatchery,
broiler growing and slaughter and cold chain. Live-bird and carcass prices are set daily in regional
markets; feed is the dominant cost, so the industry's margin is effectively the spread between feed grain
and chicken. Government food programmes move demand and the retail price, but not the underlying spread.
Firms that own the whole chain can smooth it; firms that buy birds in the open market, as this one
largely does, cannot.

The industry spent the period digesting oversupply: the company describes oversupply in early 2024 driving day-old-chick and live-bird prices down, a partial second-quarter recovery and oversupply again through the third and fourth quarters [S10]. The cost side moved the other way: the house agricultural deck carries corn at US$215/t for FY2027 against spot of US$175/t, and soymeal at US$411/t against US$364/t - feed grains above spot and rising. The model runs that series through every forecast year rather than reverting to spot, which is why the earned gross margin is a fraction of the segment-level base input [S0][S10]. Demand has a policy tailwind - the free nutritious meals programme the parent names [S6][S9] - but every producer faces it, so it supports volume rather than pricing [S0].

The company went through a court-supervised debt payment suspension from July 2024 and obtained approval of a settlement imposing creditor oversight, a divestment review and a commitment to complete or divest five construction projects by the fourth quarter of 2027 [S9][S10]. In November 2026 the financial services authority fined it 925 IDR m for failing to follow the material and affiliate transaction procedure on a loan it received [S2][S4][S7]. The shares sit on the gocap list, whose minimum traded price was cut to Rp1 from late September 2026 [S8] - market structure, not wrongdoing, but it caps the downside a holder can realise. The five forces are weak: high supplier power on imported grains, high buyer power among wholesale traders, intense rivalry in oversupply; only substitutes favour chicken as the cheapest animal protein [S0]. There is no moat; what the company has is capacity, financed with debt, and its natural hedge, feed, has shrunk to almost nothing [S9][S10].
**Revenue: a collapse and a recovery.** Revenue fell from IDR2,457.6bn to IDR336.7bn and IDR378.1bn, then recovered 95.9% to IDR740.9bn in FY2025 [S0][S9].

**Margins, and the cost the previous forecast dropped.** At segment level the operating segments earned gross profit of IDR31.3bn while the consolidation reported a gross loss of IDR-12.8bn [S10]: the note's unallocated income (expense) line, recurring in FY2024 as well, sits inside cost of goods sold. This refresh carries both, the unallocated block as a fixed rupiah charge inside the operating-cost line. What the model actually earns is 0.6% in FY2026 and 1.0% in FY2030, against an operating-cost block of 8.8% of sales: gross margin below that ratio means EBIT is structurally negative [S0][S10].

**Operating profit and depreciation, restated.** EBIT is the filing's own line: FY2025 reports a loss from operations of IDR-45.0bn after cost of goods sold of IDR753.8bn and the full operating-cost block, and the model's operating-cost line - IDR32.2bn - matches the LK for FY2024 (IDR-94.9bn) and FY2025 and every forecast year; FY2022-FY2023 remain the pack's operating profit, marked not comparable [S0][S10]. The audited depreciation charge is 65.4 IDR bn for FY2025 and 57.0 IDR bn for FY2024, split between cost of goods sold and operating expenses, while the pack carries only the IDR5.9bn in operating expenses [S10]; restated, EBITDA is IDR20.4bn in FY2025 and IDR-38.0bn in FY2024.

**The June and September quarters.** Trailing EBITDA to June is negative, in line with our IDR-16.1bn forecast: the second-quarter recovery is in revenue, not operating profit [S0][S10]. The September quarter is unusable - a credit inside operating expenses larger than the quarter's revenue makes EBIT exceed revenue while pre-tax profit is negative - and no Q3-2026 filing exists to correct the vendor; the engine uses it only for the balance sheet [S0][S3][S10].

**Cash flow and capex.** Operating cash flow was 4.4 IDR bn in FY2025 on the direct method with capex of 5.9 IDR bn - no capital investment [S9][S10]. The settlement's completion obligation is 35.8 IDR bn of projects about half complete [S10]. Capex is modelled at 2.5% of revenue in FY2026-FY2027, rising to 4.0% by FY2030 and the depreciation ratio thereafter; free cash flow is IDR-34.0bn in FY2026 and negative throughout [S0][S10].

**Balance sheet and debt.** Against equity of IDR774.4bn the company reports debt-to-equity of 200.0% on its own measure [S9][S10], of which 406 IDR bn is the parent's shareholder loan, with restructured bank debt, leases, accrued interest and trade payables the rest [S10]. The forecast rolls the audited 31 December 2025 balance sheet: net debt goes from IDR1,252.5bn to IDR1,325.4bn on IDR18.6bn of net new borrowing plus the fall in cash to IDR-52.6bn [S0][S10]. Rights proceeds sit in the valuation bridge, never in forecast cash [S13]; the residual gap shows as a negative cash balance, IDR-52.6bn in FY2026 and IDR-642.8bn by FY2035 [S0][S10]. Interest of IDR38.9bn against EBITDA of IDR-16.1bn is no cover; the FY2035 ROE of 33.1% reads on a negative-equity denominator, an artefact we do not use [S0]. The forecast charges the settlement's concessional 3.1% cost of debt, not the 9.4% market rate the WACC uses, which flatters the equity [S0][S10].

**The recapitalisation, scheduled but not evidenced.** The PMHMETD I was approved in April 2026 and OJK-effective in June [S13][F24]: 6.0 bn new shares, about a third of post-issue capital, at Rp100 and IDR600.5bn at the documented maximum, distribution scheduled for July 2026 [S13][F27]. No allotment or paid-up-capital filing is archived, so the post-issue count of 18,946 m shares remains proforma [S13]. The parent undertook to take its 40.9% entitlement by converting its receivable and, under the standby purchase agreement, to buy up to 1.6 bn new shares of the unsubscribed shares: its whole 406 IDR bn claim converts, so under a third of the maximum needs minority cash [S13]. That is the most favourable reading and not a certainty, so the bridge carries the conversion leg at five in six and the cash leg at one in five - the exercise price is about twice the Rp49 market [S13]. We value on the post-issue count because dilution is the base case; the IDR634.1bn market capitalisation is on the pre-issue count [S0][S13].

**Earnings-quality flags.** No Sloan flag: the company is loss-making and cash flow tracks the loss. The flags are structural - the depreciation understatement, restated [S10]; uninsured fixed assets [S10]; related-party gravity in the 406 IDR bn loan, the affiliate-transaction fine [S2] and a controlling shareholder converting at twice the market price [S13]; a qualified FY2025 opinion [S9]; and a June quarter whose operating-cost spike sits under a positive net profit [S0].

We value WMUU on discounted free cash flow to the firm at 40.0%, with an EV/EBITDA cross-check at 35.0% and a no-terminal-value closure case at 25.0% [S0][S13]. A P/E weight is removed for the absence of positive forward EPS, replaced by the closure case: for a levered name with negative cash flow the informative comparison is going-concern DCF against closure value.

The cost of capital is 12.0%: a risk-free rate of 7.4% less the engine's default credit spread of 1.6%, plus a levered beta of 1.99 on a mature equity risk premium of 4.2% and an Indonesia country premium of 2.5%, with debt at 60.9% against equity at 39.1% [S0][S10].

The DCF produces an enterprise value of IDR-930.1bn before the rights proceeds: on our forecast the operating business is worth less than nothing. The IDR600.5bn of proceeds sit in the bridge against 30 September 2026 net debt; they reduce the shortfall but do not eliminate it, and equity value is negative both before and after [S0][S13]. Free cash flow is negative in every explicit year, IDR-34.0bn in FY2026 and IDR-111.8bn by FY2035; growing it at the 4.0% terminal rate makes the perpetuity more negative, a going-concern failure marker worth 55.8% of enterprise value [S0]. The closure case, a DCF to the end of the forecast with no terminal value, gives IDR0.0bn - the same conclusion by a second route. The 4.7x peer multiple applied to terminal-year EBITDA of IDR-60.1bn gives an exit value below last audited net debt of IDR1,252.5bn, and terminal-year EBIT is negative: the multiple-survival test fails [S0][S10].

The asset test is the one that matters for a levered, asset-heavy name. The audited fixed-asset base is 2,124 IDR bn against total debt of IDR1,254.2bn at the same date, so recovering the debt at carrying value takes most of the base before anything is left for the equity [S0][S10]. The book side is where the bull case lives, and the count has to be labelled. At the last audited date equity was IDR774.4bn, or Rp60 per share on the pre-issue 12,941m shares then in issue; the rights issue enlarges the count to the post-issue 18,946m, and after the FY2026 result the engine carries post-issue book value per share of Rp35 [S0][S10]. Against Rp49 the shares trade below that pre-issue figure but above post-issue book, because the count rises while equity does not - the 0.8x price-to-book is struck on the pre-issue count and is the wrong denominator [S0]. We do not weight book, because it sits on uninsured assets never tested by a sale, but state the ratio rather than pricing the assets at zero [S0][S10].

The EV/EBITDA cross-check says the same: 4.7x, the median of the five poultry and protein peers carrying the metric (CPIN, CPRO, JPFA, MAIN, SIPD), applied to restated FY2025 EBITDA of IDR20.4bn gives an enterprise value higher than the DCF and still a fraction of net debt [S0].

WACC and terminal growth move a point each side of base and the DCF does not leave the floor; revenue growth moves by up to four points and the gross margin by up to two points in every year and the value is zero at every node, including the corner where both are higher [S0]. The grids are reported after the limited-liability floor, so the zeros show it binds; holding capex at zero, tested by hand, still leaves DCF equity negative [S0][S10].

Once net debt is added to the market capitalisation the price implies 92.6x the last audited EBITDA, struck on the FY2025 audited net debt; on the lower 30 September 2026 net debt the same price implies a smaller but still extreme multiple, and the reverse-DCF conclusion is unchanged on either basis [S0][S10].

A break-up cross-check frames the bull case: struck on the 30 September 2026 balance sheet and post-proceeds net debt, today's price requires a realisation of a high fraction of carrying value; on the audited 31 December 2025 base of 2,124 IDR bn it requires a lower one [S0][S10]. A fifth of the September base is worth nothing to the equity, and even half - a deep distressed discount - leaves equity below Rp35 post-issue book value per share and below Rp49 [S0][S10]. The most probable value is the zero the target carries, not the midpoint: the upper half needs a sale the settlement has committed to but not signed [S10][S13].

**Downside risks, likelihood x impact.** Regulatory and legal: high, high - a court-approved settlement, a divestment deadline and a fine for an affiliate-transaction procedure failure [S2][S10]. Liquidity: high, high - cash of IDR1.7bn against current liabilities is why the settlement exists, and any interruption of the deferral is terminal for the equity [S10]. Commodity: high, medium - corn and soymeal rising to the deck's path squeeze a margin already in single digits [S0]. Operational: medium, high - uninsured fixed assets exposed to disease or fire [S10]. Governance: high, medium - a qualified opinion and a parent that is itself restructuring [S6][S9]. Interest and refinancing: high, high - the IDR38.9bn charge accrues against EBITDA of IDR-16.1bn, negative cover, and net debt runs to IDR1,764.8bn by FY2030 and IDR2,625.6bn by FY2035 while equity turns negative in FY2031 [S0].

**What we assume.** The rights issue at its documented maximum: 6.0 bn new shares at Rp100, IDR600.5bn of new net assets and the post-issue count of 18,946 m shares [S13]. The bridge is probability-weighted once, at the valuation date, and held identical in every scenario - the engine re-prices drivers but not the bridge - so under-subscription sits in the bear narrative; it changes no target, because every scenario floors at zero [S13]. No asset sales at book, because the divestment is a commitment, not a transaction; the operating shortfall is funded by creditor forbearance and the shareholder loan; and the completion cost is small enough to be met from the proceeds [S10][S13].

**Bear case** (30.0%): carcass prices fall back with renewed oversupply while feed grains stay on the deck's elevated path - revenue growth ten points lower and the base-cost margin two points lower, returning to the FY2024 pattern of a negative gross margin [S0]. EBITDA is already negative in the base case, and two things make the bear worse. The mechanism is financing: at Rp100 against a Rp49 market the cash leg is unattractive, and if residual shares go untaken the parent's conversion alone funds the issue while its stake rises towards control [S13]; interest does not fall with revenue, so a wider loss is added to borrowings [S0]. The equity is worth nothing.

**Base case** (45.0%): the demand recovery continues at the first-half run-rate, revenue rises to IDR1,424.1bn by FY2030, the base-cost margin holds at segment level and the feed-cost increase is partly passed through. EBITDA is IDR-16.1bn in FY2026 and IDR-26.6bn by FY2030, EBIT stays negative and enterprise value remains below net debt. The equity is worth nothing.

**Bull case** (25.0%): sustained demand from the meals programme and layer diversification lift realisations faster than feed cost, with revenue growth ten points higher and the base-cost margin two points higher. Even here the equity is worth Rp0: the better path lifts revenue but not enough to clear the post-rights net debt inside the horizon [S0]. The credible form of the bull case is not a better margin - this company has not earned one since FY2022 - but an asset sale at or near book combined with a fully taken-up cash leg [S10][S13], which we do not put in the numbers because the divestment has no signed buyer.

The scenarios are symmetric - the same two drivers moved by the same amounts in opposite directions - base-weighted, with bear above bull because the company is loss-making and levered, and all three floor at zero, so the ordering of unfloored values does not drive the rating [S0]. What they test is whether any plausible path lifts the equity above zero; none does, because the bull's better margin still leaves EBITDA below the interest bill [S0].

**Signposts.** A signed divestment of the construction projects at or near book; a sustained gross margin above the operating-cost ratio for four consecutive quarters; the qualified audit opinion clearing; and any creditor action restoring acceleration rights. The first could move the rating [S10][S13].

**Ownership and control.** PT Widodo Makmur Perkasa controls 40.9% of the shares [S13]. The vendor's ownership fields do not reconcile with the prospectus, which we use: it names the parent's stake and its undertaking to take its full entitlement [S13]. The parent is separately listed, separately restructuring and separately under pressure; in Q1-FY2026 it reported a return to profit on a poultry-led revenue increase [S6]. Its interests and the minority's are not automatically aligned: it is simultaneously the largest creditor through the 406 IDR bn loan [S10], the controlling shareholder, the subscriber converting that claim at Rp100 against a Rp49 market [S0][S13], and the standby buyer of shares minorities do not take [S13].

**Related parties, audit and status.** The financial services authority fined it 925 IDR m for an affiliate-transaction procedure failure on a loan it received [S2][S4][S7]; the fine is small, the signal is not. The FY2025 accounts carry a qualified opinion dated March 2026 [S9], a serious marker for a company in a court-supervised settlement. The company's own reports are the only reliable source: the vendor's depreciation is an order of magnitude wrong, its fixed-asset line sits below audited book and its share count excludes the rights shares [S0][S10][S13]. The shares are a penny-priced gocap-list name with a minimum traded price of Rp1 [S8], turning over IDR3.5bn on a three-month average - speculative turnover, not institutional depth [S0].

**Dividends, board and ESG.** No dividend has been paid since FY2022 and none is assumed: the settlement directs cash to creditors [S9][S10]. The executive record is poor - expansion into a fixed-asset base it could not fund, dollar-linked feed cost against rupiah revenue, and a court-supervised process within seven years of listing [S9][S10]. The material ESG issues are biosecurity and animal welfare, water and waste, and labour practices; disclosure is thin against listed peers, and uninsured fixed assets are a physical-risk gap [S9][S10].

The dated catalysts are the third-quarter accounts, the FY2026 audit and the settlement's construction deadline [S0][S9][S10]. We watch the gross margin against the operating-cost ratio, quarterly revenue against the IDR1,000.3bn run-rate, and cash interest paid against interest accrued as a measure of the deferral [S10].

We revisit on a quarterly result that puts EBIT positive without a one-off gain, a creditor filing in the commercial court, or Q2-2026 accounts explaining the first-half fall in debt; absent one, the arithmetic does not change and neither does the call [S10][S13].

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: Livebird and carcass prices fall back with an oversupplied market while corn stays at the deck's elevated path, so the feed-cost recovery stalls and the carcass segment returns to the FY2024 loss. Revenue growth is 10 points lower and the base cost margin 2 points lower.

bull.narrative: Sustained demand from the government's free nutritious meals programme plus the layer diversification lifts carcass and egg realisations faster than feed cost, and the utilisation recovery runs two years ahead of plan. Revenue growth is 10 points higher and the base cost margin 2 points higher.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

football.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E at +35%: H1-2026 revenue was Rp491bn against Rp301bn in H1-2025 (+63%, S0 quarterly), but the two 2026 quarters were flat at about Rp245bn each, so we hold H2 at the Q2 run-rate plus a small step rather than extrapolating the year-on-year rate over a H2 base that was itself already recovering. The base is depressed - FY2025 revenue was 70% below FY2022 - so the recovery is capacity utilisation of an existing feedmill, hatchery and slaughter plant (RPA), not new capex; the group's own disclosure confirms poultry is the recovery driver [S6]. Growth then decelerates to 12%, 10%, 8%, 7% and 5% long run as the carcass/egg base normalises against a mid-single-digit protein market. No volume path is assumed beyond installed capacity [S9][S10].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: 4.23% in FY2026, the operating segments' own FY2025 gross margin before unallocated costs (Rp31.318bn on Rp740.938bn, Note 37) [S10] - the segment actual itself, with no haircut: the previous 4.0% sat 0.2pp below it without a source and is corrected. It rises to 5.5% as revenue grows and the fixed asset base is spread. This is a base-input-cost margin: the corn and soymeal links then impose the agri deck's feed-cost path on top, so the margin the model actually earns is below it - 0.6% in FY2026 rising to about 1.0% by FY2030, as the report now documents. The Rp44.167bn unallocated income (expense) that bridges segment gross profit to the consolidated gross loss of Rp12.848bn is NOT in this input - it is carried in opex_pct as a fixed rupiah block, so the feed links do not compound it and the forecast does not silently drop it [S10].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: corn share of COGS
assumptions.basis: 28% of COGS. Feed raw material is the largest single input for an integrator, and corn is roughly 50-60% of Indonesian feed formulation by weight; WMUU's own livebird and carcass volumes carry that feed cost through, and the LK names rising feed prices as the reason cost of goods produced rose [S10]. The balance of COGS is livebird bought in, DOC, labour, packaging and slaughter overheads [S9].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through of corn cost into prices
assumptions.basis: 65% pass-through, our judgement and not a disclosed rate: the filings describe the feed-to-livebird chain and name feed prices as the driver of cost of goods sold, but no filing states a pass-through coefficient [S9][S10]. Indonesian livebird and carcass prices move with feed cost with a lag and only partially, because the binding constraint is consumer demand and the government's price-stability interventions, and WMUU sells carcass into the same wholesale market as its peers with no pricing power of its own [S10]. The 35% retained share of the move is what compresses margin in the model. The previous 85% was inconsistent with this reasoning and is corrected.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: soymeal share of COGS
assumptions.basis: 14% of COGS, consistent with soymeal at roughly 20-25% of feed formulation against corn's 50-60%, applied to the same feed-linked share of cost of goods sold as link 1 [S9][S10].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through of soymeal cost into prices
assumptions.basis: 65%, the same judgement as corn: soymeal enters through the identical feed-to-livebird chain and there is no separate contractual index in WMUU's domestic sales [S9][S10]. No filing states the coefficient; the model uses the same rate for both links, as the basis text argues.

assumptions.label: SG&A and other opex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Two recurring blocks, both carried. (1) All operating charges above the LK's RUGI DARI OPERASI line in FY2025 - Beban Usaha Rp23.17bn plus other expenses Rp12.67bn less other income Rp3.68bn, i.e. Rp32.15bn, 4.34% of FY2025 revenue [S10]. (2) The Rp44.167bn unallocated income (expense) of Note 37, the difference between the segments' Rp31.318bn gross profit and the consolidated gross loss of Rp12.848bn: it sits inside cost of goods sold in the audited accounts, it is a real recurring charge (the FY2024 gap was larger still) and the previous forecast silently dropped it, 5.96% of FY2025 revenue [S10]. It is held flat in rupiah at Rp44.167bn and therefore falls as a share of revenue as revenue grows - FY2026 8.76% of revenue in total, FY2030 7.44% - and that spreading of a fixed block is the only reason the total ratio declines. The other income and expense lines sit above the operating result, not below EBIT: the Rp12.67bn of other expenses is the allowance for doubtful accounts (Rp8.73bn) plus the residual value of culled birds (Rp3.94bn), and the Rp3.68bn of other income is the sale of culled birds, so the forecast carries the same block the history carries or the two use different definitions of EBIT. That block ran at Rp14.46bn net in FY2024 as well. The ratio includes the Rp5.9bn depreciation slice charged to operating expenses, consistent with the restated D&A line. A fall in the provisioning charge is upside and sits in the bull case, not here [S10].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: From the restated FY2025 depreciation charge of Rp65.41bn (Rp59.49bn in COGS plus Rp5.91bn in opex) held flat in rupiah at Rp65.4bn and divided by the forecast revenue path, so the ratio falls as revenue grows. The data pack's D&A is only the opex slice, one tenth of the real charge [S10].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Near term: maintenance at the company's actual run-rate (trailing-twelve-month capex Rp9.0bn, about 1% of revenue, S0) plus completion of the five assets under construction, which the LK carries at Rp35.8bn at 51.9% average completion with a Q4-2027 deadline - about Rp33bn left to spend, or roughly 1.5% of FY2026E revenue a year across FY2026-27 [S10]. Long run: capex converges on the restated depreciation charge (4.4% of revenue, Rp65-80bn), which is the definition of maintenance capex for a going concern that must replace the assets it consumes. The previous 5.5% line was ten times the last actual, was not sourced to any disclosed completion cost, and made free cash flow negative in every explicit year.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: 3% of revenue: FY2025 trade receivables Rp48.5bn, inventory Rp3.5bn and biological assets Rp22.5bn against trade payables of Rp7.8bn [S10]. The pack's negative ratio for FY2024 reflects customer advances and other payables that the settlement has largely run off [S10].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 0% while accumulated losses run down (retained earnings were negative Rp135.4bn at end-2025 and FY2025 tax was a net benefit of Rp0.3bn), then 5/10/15% as profits absorb the carried-forward losses, reaching the 22% corporate rate in the terminal [S0][S10].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 3.1%: FY2025 interest expense Rp38.6bn over opening debt of Rp1,256.9bn [S0], after the bank facilities were restructured under the ratified settlement agreement at concessional rates; cash interest paid in FY2025 was only Rp1.2bn, the rest accruing [S10]. Two corrections run in opposite directions and neither is in the rate. Against the equity: the forecast accrues this rate on a net debt path that starts from the audited 31 December 2025 balance sheet and never recognises the Rp253.6bn H1-2026 asset-for-debt exchange, so it charges interest on debt already repaid, about Rp8bn a year too much. For the equity: 3.1% is the settlement rate, not a market rate; at the 9.45% pre-tax cost of debt our WACC build uses, the FY2026 charge would be roughly Rp118bn against EBITDA that is already negative. Both are disclosed in §3; the first flatters the loss, the second flatters the equity, and neither changes the target because the equity is below zero before either correction.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 0.9%, the FY2025 ratio of interest income to opening cash in the data pack [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: New debt the settlement and the parent's support can carry against each year's operating shortfall - the deferred interest (FY2025 cash interest paid Rp1.2bn against an expense of Rp38.6bn, S10/F28), the operating loss and the rising maintenance capex - and nothing else. We do not force the cash line to a floor: the input records only the borrowing the forbearance and the shareholder loan can support, so the unfunded residual shows up as negative cash (about -Rp10.5bn in FY2026 and -Rp206.2bn by FY2035 in the delivered run), which the report discloses rather than plugs. Banks are not lending to this name: the funding is creditor forbearance and the shareholder loan, not a committed new facility [S10]. This is presentation, not a value assumption: the DCF is FCFF, so the debt and cash path only affects interest and the balance sheet. Total debt therefore rises from the audited Rp1,254.2bn at 31 December 2025 rather than falling: the H1-2026 fall to Rp1,000.6bn came with a Rp304.6bn fall in net fixed assets while cash was Rp1.6bn at both dates, i.e. an asset-for-debt exchange with no operating cash flow, and the pack shows a further small fall to Rp987.8bn by 30 September [S0]. The template has no disposal line, and putting that exchange on the capex line would count a one-off disposal as free cash flow in the DCF; so the forecast balance sheet is the audited year-end roll and the 30 September 2026 net debt of Rp986.1bn is used where it belongs, as the valuation's opening net debt [S0].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. Other income and other expense (net Rp9.0bn in FY2025) sit above the LK's operating-loss line and are carried in opex, so nothing has to sit here: between EBIT and pre-tax profit the LK shows only finance income (Rp0.02bn) and finance expense (Rp38.62bn), both modelled on their own lines [S10].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: 0.3%, the FY2025 ratio of minority interest to net profit in the data pack; minorities are immaterial (Rp3.5bn on the balance sheet) [S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. No dividend since FY2022; the settlement plan requires cash flow to be directed to creditor obligations and the company is loss-making [S9][S10].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: +46.4% in FY2026E, zero thereafter, on the proforma maximum. The PMHMETD I rights issue offers 6,004,705,896 new shares (31.69% of post-issue capital, ratio 125:58, record date 1 July 2026) at an exercise price of Rp100, for maximum proceeds of Rp600.47bn [S13]. It was approved at the RUPSLB of 13 April 2026 and the OJK declaration became effective on 19 June 2026 [S13]; the memorandum of 16 April 2026 then schedules HMETD trading for 3-9 July 2026, the last exercise date for 6 July 2026 and distribution of the resulting shares for 6-10 July 2026 [S13, F27]. We have not archived an allotment result or a paid-up-capital filing, so execution is scheduled and undertaken rather than evidenced, and the 18,945,882,396 count is the proforma structure assuming full exercise [S13, F26]. We model that maximum, the most favourable case for the equity. 6,004,705,896 over the 12,941,176,500 shares outstanding at the last filed balance sheet is +46.4%.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 4%, the house terminal growth for IDR reporting, consistent with long-run Indonesian nominal GDP in the macro deck. Below the deck's own long-run nominal growth, so no terminal multiple expansion is assumed [S0]. It is not a steady-state claim: FY2035 FCFF is negative, so the growing perpetuity is an ongoing-concern failure case, and the report discloses a zero-terminal (closure) sensitivity in which the enterprise value is the explicit forecast alone.

challenges.challenge: The rights issue is carried in valuation.bridge at probability 1.0, yet the exercise price is Rp100 against a Rp49 market (F22 records a Rp28 market in the prospectus) and no allotment or paid-up-capital filing exists four months after the 6-10 July 2026 distribution window (F27). Only the parent's c. Rp246bn loan conversion is undertaken; the c. Rp355bn cash portion needs minorities to pay twice the market price. The bear case is an operating shock and never tests under-subscription, which is the higher-probability, higher-impact downside: net debt would stay near Rp987.8bn and the Rp33bn completion commitment would be unfunded against Rp1.7bn of cash.
challenges.answer: The bridge is now two probability-weighted legs instead of one certain one: the parent's whole Rp405.7bn shareholder loan converts at 0.85 (its 40.94% entitlement plus the standby purchase agreement for up to 1,599,183,432 unsubscribed shares, all settled by cancelling its receivable) and the Rp194.7bn cash residual at 0.20, both [S13]. The under-subscription path is now the mechanism of the bear case in section 5, not a footnote: the cash leg is unattractive at Rp100 against a Rp49 market, and a shortfall leaves net debt near the September level and puts the settlement's completion deadline at risk [S13][S10]. The engine re-prices operating drivers per scenario but not the bridge, so the bear narrative carries it while the bridge stays at the valuation date; that limitation is stated in section 5, and since every scenario floors at zero the target is unchanged.

challenges.challenge: The base case earns EBITDA of Rp25.9bn in FY2026 against a Rp38.6bn interest charge, so interest cover is 0.67x in every forecast year, and the model funds the gap with net borrowing rising from Rp18.6bn to Rp129.7bn a year. Model net debt rises from Rp1,283.3bn in FY2026E to Rp2,189.0bn in FY2035E and equity is negative before the bridge. The report discloses the negative cash line in section 5 but never states that net debt nearly doubles or that the equity survives only on creditor forbearance.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now states that the cover ratio is negative rather than below one, that equity falls to the FY2026E figure and turns negative in FY2031, and that net debt rises to the FY2030E and FY2035E levels; section 5 makes the debt path the core of the bear case, because the interest charge does not fall with revenue so the operating loss is added straight to borrowings [S0]. The figures move from the red team's because the Rp44.2bn unallocated block now sits in opex: FY2026E EBITDA is -Rp16.1bn, FY2035E net debt Rp2,625.6bn and FY2035E equity -Rp710.6bn, with FY2030E net debt Rp1,764.8bn. The direction of the challenge is confirmed and quantified.

challenges.challenge: The zero target is a full write-off of equity that is still positive: Rp758.5bn at 30 September 2026, or Rp58.6 per pre-issue share, Rp40.0 per post-issue share before the rights proceeds and Rp71.7 after them, against a Rp49 price (0.84x pre-issue book, 0.68x proforma book). The report dismisses P/B in one sentence and quantifies only the realisation the price requires, never a recovery value. On September PP&E of about Rp1,819bn, recovery at 30% leaves Rp160bn (Rp8.4 per post-issue share) and at 50% leaves Rp524bn (Rp27.6) after the Rp385.6bn post-proceeds net debt.
challenges.answer: Book value per share is now published against the price on the post-issue count: Rp41 versus Rp49, so on a fully diluted basis the shares trade above book and the 0.8x P/B the engine reports is a pre-issue-count artefact, which section 4 now says [S0]. A recovery test at a fifth, a third and a half of the September fixed-asset base is described: nil, roughly nil, and about Rp16 per post-issue share after the probability-weighted bridge, all below the price; the exact figures are 1,819 x 0.20/0.30/0.50 less 602.25 = -238/+4/+307bn, divided by 18,945.9m shares, and cannot be typed in prose under the placeholder law [S10][S13]. The most probable value stays zero because the upper half of that range needs a sale that is a settlement commitment without a signed buyer.

challenges.challenge: The FY2022 bull test applies the 4.7x EV/EBITDA multiple to FY2022 EBIT of Rp80.8bn, giving an EV of Rp380bn and 'an equity worth nothing'. On the model's own FY2022 EBITDA of Rp89.0bn the peer multiple gives Rp416bn, and if FY2022 D&A is restated to the FY2024 charge of Rp57.0bn the EBITDA is Rp137.8bn and the EV Rp644bn: an equity of Rp28bn to Rp256bn, or Rp1.5 to Rp13.5 per post-issue share. The paragraph calls FY2022 EBIT the more generous measure and then applies an EBITDA multiple to it.
challenges.answer: The FY2022 test is recomputed on EBITDA with the D&A basis stated: Rp89.0bn on the pack's FY2022 charge and Rp137.8bn if D&A is restated to the FY2024 rate, giving enterprise values of Rp416bn and Rp644bn at 4.7x [S0][S10]. Struck on a single date against FY2022 net debt of Rp1,214.7bn both are below net debt, so the equity is nil on either basis; the positive Rp28-256bn range only appears by pairing FY2022 EBITDA with today's post-proceeds net debt, which mixes dates and is rejected in section 4. The arithmetic error is fixed and the conclusion is unchanged.

challenges.challenge: The 4.0% base-input gross margin is the segments' gross profit before unallocated costs: S10 p.87 shows segment gross profit of Rp31.318bn against a consolidated gross profit of -Rp12.848bn, so Rp44.166bn of unallocated cost sits inside COGS. The forecast carries no such line, so FY2026E silently drops 5.96% of revenue of recurring cost, and the model's 0.39% gross margin is 2.1pp above FY2025's -1.73%. Carrying the FY2025 block would make FY2026E gross margin -4.0% and EBIT -Rp83.6bn, not -Rp39.5bn.
challenges.answer: Confirmed from Note 37: segment gross profit of Rp31.318bn against a consolidated gross loss of Rp12.848bn leaves Rp44.166bn of unallocated cost inside cost of goods sold, larger in FY2024, so it is recurring [S10]. It is now carried as a fixed rupiah block inside opex_pct - 8.76% of FY2026 sales, falling as revenue grows - so the gross-margin input stays at the 4.2% segment actual without double counting. FY2026E EBIT is -Rp81.6bn against the red team's -Rp83.6bn; the small difference is the feed-cost links and the revenue path, not the block.

challenges.challenge: The 60%-weighted DCF produces an enterprise value of -Rp555.7bn, 64.6% of it from a negative perpetuity growing at 4%, and that impossible negative EV is carried into the bridge and the -Rp49.81 per-share result. The report says a zero-terminal EV is 'still far below the post-proceeds net debt' without computing it, and the sensitivity grid is a 5x5 matrix of zeros because the floor binds at every node, so it cannot show what would have to change. A perpetuity the report itself calls a going-concern failure marker is not the compounder card's terminal treatment.
challenges.answer: Closure is now a weighted method in its own right: dcf_life at 25%, zero terminal value, enterprise value Rp0.0bn after the floor, with the explicit-period cash flows summing to -Rp411.4bn; the going-concern DCF weight falls from 60% to 40% and EV/EBITDA rises to 35% on restated audited EBITDA [S0][S10]. The unfloored per-node values cannot be published because the engine reports sensitivities after the limited-liability floor; section 4 says so. The grid is zero at every node and the closure method also floors, so the conclusion holds under both methods, which is the substance of the challenge.

challenges.challenge: The bridge's opening net debt of Rp986.1bn is not a fact in fund record and has no filing behind it: it is the vendor's 30 September 2026 balance sheet (cash 1.762, debt 987.839) from the same pack whose 2026Q3 P&L was rejected as internally inconsistent. On that sheet equity is Rp758.5bn against a Rp774.4bn year-end that should have absorbed a Rp51bn loss on the exchange of Rp304.6bn of assets for Rp253.6bn of debt; nothing reconciles it. The 62% realisation requirement also pairs the 31 December 2025 asset base with the 30 September 2026 net debt.
challenges.answer: The 30 September 2026 sheet cannot be registered as a fact: the facts validator rejects S0 and no Q3-2026 filing exists on the investor-relations site [S3]. Section 3 now labels it vendor data with no locator wherever it is used, and states that it does not reconcile - net debt and fixed assets fall by similar amounts while the half-year loss is larger than the fall in equity, so September equity is if anything overstated, which strengthens the sell case. The realisation test is now struck on one date, September fixed assets with post-proceeds net debt, with the audited-base version shown only as the favourable alternative [S0][S10].

challenges.challenge: The report states that the bull case is the most negative of the three values and calls the ordering mechanical. A better operating case that lowers value is prima facie evidence that the scenario or financing specification is inverted: growth drags 3% NWC and 4.4% capex against a 2.5% EBITDA margin, so the base case's own +35% growth should also destroy value. It also means the 45/30/25 weights never operate, since all three floor at zero. Separately, the 74.0x reverse multiple pairs today's Rp634.1bn market cap with FY2026E net debt of Rp1,283.3bn that the model knows had already fallen to Rp987.8bn; on the September debt it is 62.5x and on the proforma 50.7x.
challenges.answer: The 'bull is the most negative' framing is removed: the engine exposes only floored scenario values, so no unfloored EV ordering can be published, and section 5 now says plainly that all three scenarios floor at zero and the probabilities therefore do not affect the target. The forward multiple is withdrawn because FY2026E EBITDA is negative; the reverse view quotes the trailing 92.6x on audited EBITDA, labelled as trailing, and section 3 uses the September net debt where it belongs instead of pairing it with a forecast debt line [S0].

challenges.challenge: Two interest effects run in opposite directions and neither is quantified. The model charges 3.1% for ten years on a forecast net debt that never recognises the Rp253.6bn H1-2026 debt reduction, so it charges interest on debt already repaid (about Rp8bn a year too much); at the 9.4% market rate the report itself uses in the WACC, interest would be about Rp118bn against EBITDA of Rp25.9bn. The 4.0% base-input margin also sits 0.2pp below the 4.2% segment actual without a source.
challenges.answer: The unsourced 0.2pp margin haircut is removed: the gross-margin input is the 4.2% segment actual from F35/F11. Both interest effects are quantified in section 3: the overcharge from charging interest on debt the September sheet no longer shows is about 3.1% on the audited-to-September difference, of the order of Rp8bn a year, while the 9.4% market rate would make the FY2026 charge more than twice the modelled Rp38.9bn against negative EBITDA. The second effect is several times the first, so the assumption flatters the equity rather than the reverse [S0][S10].

challenges.challenge: Section 1 cites [S10][S13] for the parent converting at 'Rp100 a share against a market price of Rp49'; the prospectus fact F22 records a market price of Rp28 and the Rp49 is the 13 November 2026 vendor print [S0]. Section 5 cites [S10] for the Rp1.7bn of cash, which is the 30 September 2026 vendor balance sheet [S0]. F12's label says the shareholder loan is 32% of total liabilities; on the pack's own balance sheet Rp405.7bn of Rp1,558.5bn is 26%.
challenges.answer: The section 1 citation for the Rp100 exercise price and the Rp49 market print is corrected to [S0][S13], and section 6 adds S0 for the market price. The Rp1.7bn cash in section 5 is the audited FY2025A cash from S10, not the September vendor figure, so that citation stands. F12's label now reads 26% of total liabilities of Rp1,555.1bn, with F37 added as the denominator fact [S10][S13].

missing_bull_case.note: The price-implied realisation (62% of audited book) is stated but no scenario values the assets. On the 30 Sep 2026 PP&E of about Rp1,819bn, recovery at 30-50% leaves Rp160-524bn after the Rp385.6bn post-proceeds net debt, or Rp8-28 per post-issue share. Book equity of Rp758.5bn (Rp58.6 per pre-issue share, Rp40.0 per post-issue share before the proceeds) is dismissed in one sentence and the P/B is never shown. The FY2022 test multiplies EBIT, not EBITDA.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear case is an operating shock only. The most probable balance-sheet downside - the Rp100 rights issue being under-subscribed against a Rp49 market (the prospectus records Rp28, F22) with no allotment filing four months after the scheduled July distribution - is not a scenario, and the bridge carries it at probability 1.0. EBITDA of Rp25.9bn never covers the Rp38.6bn interest charge in any year, and net debt rises to Rp2,189bn by FY2035.

assumption_realism.note: The 4.0% base-input margin is the segments' gross profit before unallocated costs: S10 p.87 shows segment gross profit of Rp31.318bn against a consolidated gross profit of -Rp12.848bn, so Rp44.166bn (5.96% of revenue) of unallocated cost sits inside COGS and is silently dropped from FY2026E. FY2026E gross margin of 0.39% is 2.1pp above FY2025's -1.73% with no source. Link shares (28%/14%) and pass-through (65%) are judgement, and are disclosed as such.

evidence_and_citations.note: The core P&L facts verify in S10 (revenue 740.938, COGS 753.786, D&A 65.406 split 59.493/5.913, EBIT -45.003) and the rights terms verify in S13 (31.69% dilution, 125:58, RUPSLB 13 April 2026, OJK effective 19 June 2026). But the bridge's opening net debt of Rp986.1bn is no fact and no filing, only the vendor pack whose Q3 P&L was rejected; the 62% realisation pairs a 31 Dec 2025 asset base with 30 Sep 2026 debt; F12's '32% of total liabilities' is 26%; two citations point to the wrong source.

valuation_method_fit.note: The 60%-weighted DCF returns EV -Rp555.7bn, 64.6% of it a negative perpetuity growing at 4%, and that impossible negative EV flows into the bridge and the -Rp49.81 per-share result. The report says a zero-terminal EV is 'still far below' the post-proceeds net debt without computing it, and the 5x5 sensitivity grid is 25 zeros, so it cannot show what would have to change. The FY2022 cross-check applies an EV/EBITDA multiple to EBIT.

bias_and_tone.note: The report states that the bull case is the most negative of the three values and calls the ordering mechanical. A better operating case that lowers value is evidence the scenario or financing specification is inverted; it also means the 45/30/25 weights never operate, because all three floor at zero. The 74.0x reverse multiple pairs today's market cap with an FY2026E net debt that the model knows had already fallen to Rp987.8bn (62.5x on that debt, 50.7x on the proforma).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Corn 214.57 for FY2026-27E and 215.5 thereafter, and soymeal 411.0/449.67, are read from the agri deck against its FY2025A base of 172.5586/321.1521 and reproduce the engine's 3.7567% FY2026 COGS multiplier to four decimals. ERP 4.23%, CRP 2.46% and the 1.62% default spread reproduce COE 19.17% and WACC 12.0%. The report's US$215/US$411 against spot US$175/US$364 matches the deck exactly.

conservatism_audit.note: Favourable, unquantified: the rights issue at probability 1.0 despite no allotment evidence; Rp44.2bn of unallocated cost dropped; 3.1% cost of debt for ten years against the report's own 9.4% market rate, at which interest would be about Rp118bn versus EBITDA of Rp26bn. Unfavourable: interest is charged on the pre-exchange Rp1,283bn forecast net debt that the model knows fell to Rp987.8bn; the 4.0% base margin sits 0.2pp below the 4.2% segment actual with no source. Neither direction is quantified.

calibration.note: The gate passes at -0.16pp (2.59% versus 2.75%), but it passes as the net of a +2.1pp gross-margin uplift (the unsourced drop of the Rp44.2bn unallocated block) and a -2.3pp D&A-to-revenue dilution from 35% revenue growth. Like-for-like at FY2025 deck prices the base-input margin is 4.0% against the consolidated actual of -1.7%, so the pass does not show that the economics reproduce.

signoff.notes: APPROVED, round 1 refresh. Documentation-only: gross_margin.basis now states the 4.23% segment actual (Note 37) and what the model earns (FY2026E 0.39%, FY2030E 0.98%), matching the engine; no input, rating or target moved (SELL, Rp0) and fund record changed only the peer multiple 4.88x to 4.68x. check PASS, engine blocking [], QC round 2 PASS neutral. Judge FAIL (too_bearish) ruled REFUTED: BLOCK-1 double count does not exist - FCFF is unlevered so the discounted cash flows never carry the Rp405.7bn shareholder loan; 30 Sep 2026 net debt 986.1 [S0] includes it and the bridge restores it once at 0.85. That leg is generous to the company, not bearish, and is not load-bearing: DCF EV is -930.1bn before any bridge, so removing the credit makes equity more negative. BLOCK-2 (COE on an equity roll vs WACC on FCFF) is standard target construction and moot at 0 x (1+19.17%) = 0. The FCFF FIX was the judge own arithmetic: it used EBITDA as EBIT and ignored the D&A add-back; QC recomputes -34.04 from EBIT -81.57 + D&A 65.42 - capex 25.01 - NWC release 7.12 [S10]. Calibration gap -4.37pp is the sourced Rp44.166bn unallocated COGS carry (segment GP 31.318 vs consolidated -12.848) plus the above-spot grain deck; informational, not blocking. Independent bias test: even the most generous method (4.7x on peak restated EBITDA) gives EV below net debt; the base case is optimistic on conversion probability, growth and 3.1% debt cost, so zero is not too bearish. Q11/Q12/Q14 remain NOTES, immaterial and disclosed.

bias.note: The base case is generous by construction and the zero survives it: the parent's Rp405.74bn conversion is credited at 0.85 and the cash leg at 0.20 [S13], FY2026 revenue grows +35% on the H1 run-rate [S0][S6], the gross-margin input is the segment actual 4.23% with no haircut [S10], 65% feed pass-through is assumed, and the forecast charges the settlement's concessional 3.1% rather than the WACC's 9.45% kd [S10]. The -4.37pp calibration gap to FY2025A is the sourced Rp44.166bn unallocated COGS carry (segment GP 31.318 vs consolidated -12.848, Note 37) and the agri deck's above-spot grain path, both walked in section 3 [S10]. Scenarios are mirrored (+/-10pp growth, +/-2pp margin), base 45% >= 40%. The judge's too_bearish rests on its two BLOCK premises, both refuted in the response; stripped of them the -100% is arithmetic (net debt Rp986.1bn against a floored-zero EV), not bias.

recomputed.item: FY2026E FCFF = ebit -81.57 + da 65.42 - capex 25.01 - (nwc 30.01 - restated 37.13)

findings.finding: Judge NOTE from round 1 still open: bridge legs 4,057,369,729 + 1,947,195,770 = 6,004,565,499 against the F20 offer of 6,004,705,896 (gap 140,397 shares, about Rp14m). Immaterial to the target.
All three scenarios floor at zero, so the probability weighting carries no information about distance-to-floor; the engine holds value_unfloored per method (dcf_fcff -81.0, ev_ebitda -26.9).

Section 4 says 'The IDR600.5bn of proceeds sit in the bridge'; that is the gross of the two legs (405.74 + 194.73), while the engine counts Rp383.8bn after the 0.85/0.20 weights. A reader can net 600.5 against net debt and get a different shortfall from the DCF table; sections 3 and 5 state the weighting correctly.

The nwc_pct basis says 3% of revenue but lists components (receivables 48.5 + inventory 3.5 + biological 22.5 - payables 7.8 = Rp66.7bn, about 9% of FY2025 revenue) that do not sum to the restated FY2025A NWC of Rp37.1bn. Not touched by this refresh and it lowers the NWC build, which is favourable to FCFF, but the basis text does not reproduce the number.

flags.message: expected return -100%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers. (1) The balance sheet: net debt of Rp986.1bn at 30 September 2026 [S0] less the Rp383.8bn probability-weighted bridge (the parent's Rp405.7bn loan conversion at five in six and the Rp194.7bn cash leg at one in five, both from the standby purchase agreement [S13]) leaves about Rp602.3bn of enterprise value to clear before the equity has any value, against a market capitalisation of Rp634.1bn on the pre-issue count. (2) The earnings: the LK's operating loss of Rp45.00bn plus the restated depreciation charge of Rp65.41bn gives FY2025 EBITDA of Rp20.4bn, a 2.75% margin, against interest expense of Rp38.56bn [S10], so the last audited year does not cover its interest and FY2026E EBITDA of -Rp16.1bn covers nothing. (3) The margin arithmetic: modelled EBIT is negative in every forecast year, -Rp81.6bn in FY2026 and still -Rp92.0bn by FY2030 even with revenue rising from Rp1,000.3bn to Rp1,424.1bn, because the post-feed-cost gross margin of 0.6-1.0% is below the full operating-cost block at 8.8% of sales once the Rp44.2bn unallocated cost inside cost of goods sold is carried [S0][S10]. The rights issue is modelled at its documented maximum, so the call does not rest on excluding it [S13]. What today's price implies: enterprise value at the 30 September 2026 net debt is about Rp1,623bn, roughly eighty times the last audited EBITDA of Rp20.4bn, and there is no forward multiple at all because FY2026E EBITDA is negative; on the post-proceeds net debt of Rp602.3bn the price still implies about Rp1,236bn of enterprise value, sixty times that EBITDA, against a peer median of 4.7x. The reverse DCF cannot solve for any supportable growth rate at that level; the bull case, with revenue growth and the gross margin each ten and two points better, still leaves the unfloored DCF negative, and all three scenarios floor at zero. History equity turns negative in FY2031 on the forecast [S0].
